nilpotentny ideal

Iztočnik / Source: nilpotentes Ideal

Rusky / Russian: нильпотентный идеал

Ukrajinsky / Ukrainian: нільпотентний ідеал

Razlog: Nilpotentny ideal čuva internacionalny algebraičny termin. Oba arhivne razloga prědpočitajut tu osnovu, s ruskym i ukrajinskym paralelami, prěd tvorjenjem nezasvědčenogo slovjanskogo neologizma; nijeden takovy neologizm ne jest imenovany kako stvarno razsmotrěna alternativa. Definicija §12 raboty 34 zahtěvaje jednu pozitivnu stepen cělogo ideala, \(\mathfrak c^\rho=0\). To jest silnějše uslovje než samo zahtěvanje, aby vsaky element iměl někoj stepen ravny nuli. Definicija vključaje nulovy ideal. Zato tvrđenje §25, že diskriminant jest nula pri obstojanju nilpotentnogo ideala, potrěbuje kontekstnu ogradu: pokazany dokaz davaje nulovy red v matricě samo pri nenulovom idealu. Dostupna rečenija ne piše nenulovy. Ostava otvorjeno, jest li to izpuščeno uslovje v prěvodu ili historična konvencija iztočnika; tu ne jest učinjena tiha ispravka.

Reason: Nilpotentny ideal retains an international algebraic term. Both preserved reasons favor this stem, with Russian and Ukrainian parallels, over an unattested Slavic neologism; neither names such a neologism as an actually considered alternative. The definition in §12 of Paper 34 requires one positive power of the whole ideal to vanish, \(\mathfrak c^\rho=0\). This is stronger than merely requiring some power of each individual element to vanish. The definition includes the zero ideal. Consequently, the §25 assertion that the discriminant vanishes when a nilpotent ideal exists needs a contextual qualification: the displayed proof supplies a zero matrix row only when the ideal is nonzero. The available sentence does not say nonzero. Whether this is an omitted translation hypothesis or a historical source convention remains unresolved; no silent emendation is made here.

Sravnjenje s tekstom: Definicija uključaje nulovy ideal. Dokaz tvrđenja o diskriminantu potrěbuje nenulovy ideal; dostupna formulacija ostava iztočnym pytanjem.

Textual comparison: The definition includes the zero ideal. The discriminant argument needs a nonzero ideal; the available wording remains a source question.

Noetherov fundamentalny teorem algebraičnyh funkcij

Iztočnik / Source: Noetherscher Fundamentalsatz der algebraischen Funktionen

Rusky / Russian: основная теорема Нётер об алгебраических функциях

Ukrajinsky / Ukrainian: Нетерова основна теорема алгебраїчних функцій

Razlog: Noetherov fundamentalny teorem algebraičnyh funkcij jest historično ime teoremy, ne obče pohvala njezinoj važnosti. Zapis prědpočita fundamentalny teorem za medžuslovjansky naslov; ruska i ukrajinska paralela upotrěbjajut prirodnu konstrukciju s osnovnoj teoremoju. V dostupnom naslově stoji Neterovomu, dokolě bibliografičny citat čuva Max Noether. Tekst i citat jasno pokazyvajut, že imenovany teorem jest Maksov, ne Emmyjin teorem o simetrijah. Rabota jest podpisana H. Kapfererom i ima dodatok sovměstny s E. Noether. Prinaležnost polinoma idealu, generovanomu dvoma polinomami, svęzuje se tu s konečnymi lokalnymi uslovjami. Takovo kratko objasnjenje pomaga identifikovati imenovany rezultat bez zaměny avtorstva i bez tvrdženja, že sam naslov davaje polny algoritm.

Reason: Noetherov fundamentalny teorem algebraičnyh funkcij is the historical name of a theorem, not general praise for its importance. The record favors fundamentalny teorem in the Interslavic title, while the Russian and Ukrainian comparanda use natural constructions with fundamental or basic theorem. The available title has Neterovomu, whereas the bibliographic citation preserves Max Noether. Text and citation make clear that the named theorem is Max’s, not Emmy’s theorem concerning symmetries. The paper is signed by H. Kapferer and includes a supplement jointly with E. Noether. Membership of a polynomial in an ideal generated by two polynomials is related here to finite local conditions. This short identification distinguishes the named result and its authorship without claiming that the title itself supplies a complete algorithm.

Sravnjenje s tekstom: Naslov, podpis, historično objasnjenje i bibliografičny citat vměstě identifikujut teorem i razlikujut avtory.

Textual comparison: The title, byline, historical explanation, and bibliographic citation together identify the theorem and distinguish the authors.

norma

Iztočnik / Source: Norm

Rusky / Russian: норма

Ukrajinsky / Ukrainian: норма

Razlog: Norma jest v zapisě prijeta kako internacionalna osnova, s ruskym i ukrajinskym norma i s padežnoju formoju normoju v medžuslovjanskom tekstu. V rabotě 31, §4, avtor imenuje normoju koeficient svobodny od \(t\) v determinantu \(|tE-C|\). Dlja matrice reda \(s\) to jest \((-1)^s\det C\), v tekstu zapisano \(\pm|C|\). To znamenje ne trěba tiho odstraniti zaradi drugoj moderne konvencije normy. Vertikalne črty tu označajut determinant, ne absolutnu cěnnost; norma ne jest po definiciji nenegativna měra dliny. Sačuvane objašnjenja izbora dlja vseh trěh jezykov napisane sut po-anglijsky. Nynějšnje medžuslovjansko objasnjenje rekonstruuje te razloge; ne pripisuje arhivu tekst na jezyku, na ktorom on ne byl napisan.

Reason: Norma is adopted in the record as an international stem, with Russian and Ukrainian norma and the inflected Interslavic normoju in the running text. In Paper 31, §4, the author calls the coefficient independent of \(t\) in \(|tE-C|\) the norm. For a matrix of order \(s\) this is \((-1)^s\det C\), written \(\pm|C|\) in the text. That sign must not be silently discarded to match another modern norm convention. The vertical bars denote a determinant, not an absolute value; the norm is not by definition a nonnegative measure of length. The preserved explanations of the choice for all three languages are written in English. The present Interslavic explanation reconstructs those reasons; it does not attribute to the archive a text in a language in which it was not written.

Sravnjenje s tekstom: Avtor oprědělja normu prěz ukazany harakterističny determinant. To fiksuje takože konvenciju znamenja.

Textual comparison: The author defines the norm through the stated characteristic determinant. This also fixes the sign convention.

norma / elementarny dělitelj

Ukrajinsky / Ukrainian: норма / елементарний дільник

Razlog: Norma i elementarny dělitelj sut različne, povezane pojmy, ne sinonimy. Arhivny razlog za dělitelj jest semantična jasnost i kontinuitet s ranějšej terminologijeju korpusa; ruska i ukrajinska paralela imaju odgovarjajuče osnovy. V rabotě 25 norma ideala jest oprěděljena posrědstvom produktov elementarnyh děliteljev modulov, pri čem samo konečno mnogo faktorov razlikujut se od jedinicy. To ne jest avtomatično norma elementa iz drugyh rabot. Pri prostom idealu tekst različa normu od najvyššego elementarnogo dělitelja: nad nedoskonalym poljem norma može byti stepen odgovarjajučej proste funkcije. Zato zaměna normy jednym elementarnym děliteljem bez ukazanogo uslovja izgubila by informaciju o mnogokratnosti. Opis izboru ne pripisuje slovu norma jedno isto oprěděljenje prěz cěly korpus.

Reason: Norma and elementarny dělitelj are distinct, related concepts, not synonyms. The archival reason for dělitelj is semantic transparency and continuity with earlier corpus terminology; the Russian and Ukrainian comparanda have corresponding stems. In Paper 25 the norm of an ideal is defined through products of elementary divisors of modules, with only finitely many factors different from the unit. It is not automatically the norm of an element used in other papers. For a prime ideal the text distinguishes its norm from its highest elementary divisor: over an imperfect field the norm may be a power of the associated irreducible polynomial. Replacing the norm by a single elementary divisor without the specified qualification would lose multiplicity information. The explanation of the lexical choice therefore does not impose one definition of norm throughout the corpus.

Sravnjenje s tekstom: Polje koeficientov, konečnost nejediničnyh faktorov i možno pojavjenje stepenov sut česti definicije i priměnjenja normy.

Textual comparison: The coefficient field, finiteness of nonunit factors, and possible appearance of powers belong to the definition and use of the norm.

Razlika od normalizacije ili normovanja slěduje iz konkretnogo matematičnogo postupa; zapis ne davaje spisok odvrgnutyh sinonimov. Dobytaja simetrična funkcija vyražaje se prěz koeficienty produkta dvou form. Konstrukcija potom davaje polinomnu identičnost, upotrěbjanu pri specializaciji. Slovarny zapis dolžen čuvati ty koeficientne polja i način tvorjenja konjugatov: opis konkretnogo produkta ne jest neograničena definicija normy dlja vsakego algebraičnogo razširjenja. Ruske postrojenije i ukrajinske pobudova sut paralely dlja konstrukcijnoj funkcii frazy, ne novi sinonimy dlja samoj normy.

Reason: Obrazovanje normy denotes the operation, norma its result. The archival record retains norma in all three translations and chooses obrazovanje for the construction step in Paper 20. The distinction from normalization follows from the actual mathematical operation; the record does not supply a list of rejected synonyms. In item 4 the author forms a linear expression \(\zeta(u)\) and multiplies it by the distinct conjugates obtained by permuting the specified rows of variables. The resulting symmetric function is expressed through the coefficients of the product of two forms. The construction then supplies a polynomial identity used under specialization. The dictionary must preserve the coefficient fields and the specified formation of conjugates: this particular product is not an unrestricted definition of norm for every algebraic extension. Russian postroenie and Ukrainian pobudova are parallels for the constructive function of the phrase, not new synonyms for the norm itself.

Textual comparison: The conjugates arise from specified permutations; the resulting identity continues to specialized values.

Arhivny razlog čuva tu vez medžu idealami i modulami: to ne jest nova, nezavisna definicija čislovoj normy. Definicija VI nazyvaje rezultat rezultantom odgovarjajučego nivoja; produkt rezultantov tvori rezultantnu formu. Ruske otnositeljno i ukrajinske vidnosno izražajut relaciju, ne operaciju děljenja. Reason: The norm of the basic ideal in Paper 22, §5, is the norm of the basic module relative to the module of the given ideal, after adjoining the specified variables to the coefficient field. Definition VI calls the result the resultant at the corresponding level, and the product of these resultants forms the resultant form. Russian otnositelno and Ukrainian vidnosno express a relation, not division. The archived vzhodno k was an earlier choice explicitly awaiting further review; the current text uses po odnošenju k. Its preservation documents the earlier decision, not a recommendation to revive the superseded construction. The symbol \(m\) names an ideal, not a unit of measurement.

Textual comparison: Definition VI links the level-\(i\) resultant to a module norm after a specified adjunction. Ideal and module language thus describe the same construction in two forms. Reading po odnošenju k preserves the order of the arguments; the resultant and greatest elementary divisor are not interchangeable.

In Paper 18 the norm is first relative to the given module and subsequently, when an ideal is decomposed into a primary component and its complement, relative to the component \(Q\). This is neither the norm of \(Q\) alone nor an ordinary remainder on division. The preposition must be read with the definitions of the modules and the adjoined coefficients. Russian po and Ukrainian za illustrate different ways of expressing the relation, but do not independently establish the broad construction as accepted Interslavic usage. The later po odnošenju k makes the relation more explicit; replacing it requires checking the arguments of the norm, not merely replacing a preposition.

V cěločislnom slučaju ona izražaje čislo ostatkovyh klasov; v polinomnom slučaju s dimenzijeju prostora klasov sravnjaje se jej stepenj, ne sam polinom. In the integer case it gives the number of residue classes; in the polynomial case its degree, not the polynomial itself, is compared with the dimension of the space of classes. The recorded reason preserves continuity with the introduction and provisionally retains vzhodno k, expressly marked for further review. normalna forma

Iztočnik / Source: Normalform

Rusky / Russian: нормальная форма

Razlog: Četyri zachovane razlogy dlja normalna forma naglašajut prozračnost kognatov i čuvanje kratkogo termina v formulah. Jednako isto nazvanje ne jest dovoljnym razlogom dlja jednake definicije v vseh rabotah. Dlja logičnogo teksta možno zadržati nazvanje, ale konjunktivna, disjunktivna ili druga normalna forma potrěbuje vlastnu definiciju i dokaz točno tvrdžene ekvivalencije.

Paper 16 also concerns selection of a representative modulo the ideal of relations between coordinates, with additional conditions on the coefficients. The adjective normalna alone does not imply a general uniqueness theorem. A logic text may retain the name, but conjunctive, disjunctive or other normal forms require their own definitions and proofs of the precise equivalence asserted.

The archival description mentions local class field theory, but the particular theorem in Paper 39 passes from all local conditions to a global conclusion. In the cyclic case an element of the ground number field is a norm from the extension if it is a norm at every finite and infinite place. The algebraic formulation concerns splitting and has its own scope. The statement cannot be transferred without its hypotheses to an arbitrary extension; Paper 38 itself marks the limit of a nonabelian generalization. The Russian and Ukrainian lettering in the archived comparanda is lost. The dictionary therefore grounds its explanation in the readable reason and actual assertions, not invented restorations of those parallels.

A note distinguishes an earlier sufficient condition from the present necessity and sufficiency. The conjunction i is therefore not interchangeable with ili. Where the conditions form a system, both implications concern the whole system; it does not follow that each condition alone is sufficient. This also matters for translation of logic: the compact phrase must retain the scope of the conditions and assertion, not weaken necessity into practical usefulness.

nula / jedinica / vlastne oblasti cělosti

Iztočnik / Source: Null / Einheit / eigentliche Integritätsbereiche

Rusky / Russian: нуль / единица / собственные области целостности

Razlog: Nula, jedinica i vlastna oblast cělosti ne sut tri zamenime nazvanja. Arhivny razlog čuva razliku medžu osnovnym pojmom prstena i silnějšimi uslovjami. V rabotě 19, §1, zakony davajut nulu, ale ne potrěbujut jedinicu ni izključenje nulovyh děliteljev. Vlastne oblasti cělosti imajut jedinicu i svojstvo, že iz nule produkta slěduje nula jednogo faktora. Jedinica tu jest neutralny element množenja, ne libovoljny obratimy element. Vlastny v istorickom nazvanju ne označaje vlastnu podmnožinu někoj drugoj oblasti. Nynějšnja definicija inogo teksta može izrično dodati \(0\ne1\); ne trěba tvrditi, že takovo dopolnjenje bylo izraženo v toj rečenici Noether. Čisla v zapisu \(na\) tu označajut povtoreno složenje, ne už zadano vloženje cělyh čisel v prsten.

Reason: Nula, jedinica and vlastna oblast cělosti are not interchangeable names. The recorded reason preserves the distinction between the underlying notion of ring and stronger requirements. In Paper 19, §1, the laws supply zero but require neither an identity nor exclusion of zero divisors. Vlastne oblasti cělosti have an identity and the property that a zero product forces one factor to be zero. Jedinica here means the multiplicative identity, not an arbitrary invertible element. Vlastny in the historical name does not mean a proper subset of another domain. Another text’s modern definition may expressly add \(0\ne1\); this must not be represented as an explicit requirement in this sentence of Noether’s. Integers in \(na\) here denote repeated addition, not an already specified embedding of the integers into the ring.

Sravnjenje s tekstom: Zakony osnovnogo prstena ne vključajut jedinicu. Tekst dodavaje ju vměstě s uslovjem o nulovom produktu, kogda nazyvaje vlastne oblasti cělosti. Čislovy množitelj \(n\) v \(na\) označaje povtoreno složenje; on ne potvrdžaje, že osnovny prsten sodrživa kopiju prstena cělyh čisel.

Textual comparison: The underlying ring laws do not include an identity. The text adds one together with the zero-product condition when naming eigentliche Integritätsbereiche. The numerical multiplier \(n\) in \(na\) denotes repeated addition; it does not establish that the ring contains a copy of the integers.

Razlog: Nulovy ideal jest ideal, sostoječi samo iz nuly. Arhivny razlog čuva to nazvanje v cěloj teoriji razloženja raboty 31; on ne predlagaje novy pojem. Iz odgovarjajučego razloženja dobyvajut se direktne komponenty prstena i izomorfizmy s prstenami ostatkovyh klasov. To ne znači, že sam prsten jest nulovy: nula jest idealom v prsteně, ktory može iměti mnoho elementov. Takože ne možno izrěkti ravnost produkta i prěsěčenja dlja libovoljnyh idealov bez uslovij. The corresponding decomposition yields direct components of the ring and isomorphisms with residue-class rings. This does not mean that the ring itself is zero: zero is an ideal in a ring that may have many elements. Nor may equality of product and intersection be asserted for arbitrary ideals without the relevant hypotheses. Russian nulevoy and Ukrainian nulovyi provide close parallels, but the principal reason for retaining the term is its clear and stable object reference in the proof.

Sravnjenje s tekstom: Produkt i prěsěčenje primarnyh idealov v toj situaciji davajut nulu, a odgovarjajuče komponenty davajut direktnu sumu prstena. Nulovy ideal ne jest isto kako nulovy prsten. Formuly i uslovja razloženja, ne samo slovo nulovy, oprěděljajut, kogda ty ravnosti imajut město.

Textual comparison: In this setting the product and intersection of the primary ideals give zero, while the corresponding components give a direct sum of the ring. A zero ideal is not a zero ring. Poslě odstranjenja vseh polinomnyh prěmennyh poslednji ideal leži v polju koeficientov i zato jest nulovy ili jediničny. Bez tyh uslovij ne možno zaključiti, že vsaka oblast cělosti jest osnovnym poljem. Pridavnik prosty ima idealno-teoretičny smysl, podprěty ruskoju i ukrajinskoju paraleloju, ne značenje lahky. Slovarny zapis čuva točnost predikata, bo proměna od jest prosty do ima prosty ideal proměnila by hipotezu dokaza.

Reason: Here nulovy ideal and prosty ideal do not form a disjunction. The hypothesis says that the zero ideal itself is prime. The recorded reason expressly rejects introducing an associated prime, which would assert something different. Paper 31, §6, treats this case over an algebraically closed ground field and in the finite-rank setting; those assumptions imply that the ring is the ground field itself. Without them, one cannot conclude that every integral domain is its ground field. Prosty has its ideal-theoretic sense, supported by the Russian and Ukrainian parallels, not the meaning easy. The dictionary preserves the exact predicate: changing is prime to has a prime ideal would change the proof’s hypothesis.

Sravnjenje s tekstom: Uslovje jest prostota samogo nulovogo ideala, ne bytje priradženogo prostogo ideala. Vyvod o rangu 1 upotrěbjaje konečny rang i algebraičnu zamknjenost osnovnogo polja. Vytrgnuta iz tyh hipotez fraza dala by mnogo silnějše i nepravdivo tvrdženje.

Textual comparison: The condition is primality of the zero ideal itself, not the existence of an associated prime. The rank-one conclusion uses finite rank and algebraic closedness of the ground field. Detached from those hypotheses, the phrase would assert something much stronger and false.

The formula using \(m-em\) explains why every ring element annihilates the second part. Zero operator and identity operator are therefore different actions on a module, not two names for the same zero object.

In Paper 19, §12, a polynomial must vanish at all finite zeros of the ideal, not just one. Likewise, if a product vanishes on the whole zero set of a prime ideal, one factor vanishes on that whole set; this is not merely a different choice of factor at each point. Textual comparison: Paper 19, §12, explicitly refers to all finite zeros and an algebraically closed range of values. Ideal membership does not follow from vanishing at one point.
